question.text: Will EU member states approve the screening results for Ukraine's accession clusters 4 and 5 before January 1, 2027?
question.resolution_criteria: This question resolves as **Yes** if, before January 1, 2027, according to credible sources Ukraine receives approval from [Coreper](https://www.consilium.europa.eu/en/council-eu/how-the-work-in-the-council-is-organised/what-is-coreper/) for the screening results for EU [Cluster 4](https://em-al.org/en/cluster-4/) and [Cluster 5](https://enlargement.ec.europa.eu/document/download/a9099136-b301-458e-a846-c6bf8c47d287_en).

research:
## 1. Resolution source

- The question resolves on credible reports that Coreper (the committee of EU ambassadors) has approved the screening results for Ukraine's clusters 4 and 5. There is no single official data page for this. In practice the step shows up in Ukrainian outlets (European Pravda) citing EU diplomats, and sometimes in Council communications.
- Coreper normally acts after the enlargement working party (COELA) clears the results. For clusters 2 and 3, COELA and Coreper both approved on the same day and invited Ukraine to present its negotiating positions. [European Pravda](https://www.eurointegration.com.ua/eng/news/2026/10/7/7247137/)
- 2026-11-10 (latest status): COELA did not approve the results for clusters 4 and 5, so nothing has gone to Coreper. I found no report of Coreper approval.

## 2. Current status

- Nothing has settled the question. Hungary is still blocking at the working-party level. An EU diplomat described its position as "No change." Moldova's clusters 4 and 5 are blocked too. [Ukrainska Pravda](https://www.pravda.com.ua/eng/news/2026/11/10/8062207/), [European Pravda](https://www.eurointegration.com.ua/news/2026/11/10/7249710/)
- Clusters 4 and 5 are the last two of Ukraine's six clusters that are still unopened.

## 3. Recent news (newest first)

- 2026-11-10: Hungary blocked the screening results for clusters 4 and 5 at COELA, its third refusal since October 20. [NV](https://english.nv.ua/nation/hungary-continues-to-stall-ukraine-s-eu-accession-talks-50658084.html), [ZMINA](https://zmina.info/en/news-en/hungary-again-blocks-screening-results-for-two-clusters-in-ukraines-eu-accession-talks/)
- 2026-11-04: Deputy PM Vsevolod Chentsov said Hungary is not raising new demands on minority rights. Budapest says it needs more time to study the documents. [European Pravda](https://www.eurointegration.com.ua/news/2026/11/10/7249710/)
- 2026-11-03: Ukraine's EU envoy Taras Kachka said there are "no substantive requirements, disagreements or concerns" from Hungary, and he expects clusters 4 and 5 to open by the end of 2026. [European Pravda](https://www.eurointegration.com.ua/eng/news/2026/11/3/7249180/)
- Around late October/November: Ukraine's foreign ministry said a Ukraine-Hungary intergovernmental commission would start work in November to discuss the blocked clusters. I could not open the article to get a date. [sud.ua](https://sud.ua/en/news/ukraine/376336-ukraina-ta-uhorshchyna-hotuiut-zasidannia-mizhuriadovoi-komisii-cherez-blokuvannia-perehovornykh-klasteriv-shchodo-vstupu-do-ies)
- 2026-10-27: Hungary refused again. One diplomat said the discussion was mainly meant to put pressure on Budapest. [Ukrainska Pravda](https://www.pravda.com.ua/eng/news/2026/10/27/8059933/)
- 2026-10-20: Hungary's first refusal on clusters 4 and 5; Forbes.ua reported that no specific conditions were named. [Forbes.ua](https://forbes.ua/news/ugorshhina-vidmovilasia-sxvaliti-skrining-klasteriv-4-ta-5-dlia-ukrayini-konkretnix-umov-ne-nazivaiut-20102026-43127)
- 2026-10-13: Clusters 2 and 3 opened after Ukraine's parliament passed minority-language education amendments. [Euronews](https://www.euronews.com/2026/10/12/ukraine-passes-minority-rights-law-paving-way-for-breakthrough-in-eu-accession-talks)

## 4. Base rates (how Hungary has handled earlier clusters in 2026)

- Background: Hungary's new prime minister, Péter Magyar, agreed an 11-point minority-rights plan with Ukraine in June. A Hungarian government representative has said Budapest opposes any "fast-track procedure" for Ukraine. [Euronews](https://www.euronews.com/my-europe/2026/06/29/explainer-why-peter-magyar-is-reluctant-to-align-with-the-eu-on-ukraine), [Euromaidan Press](https://euromaidanpress.com/2026/07/14/magyar-hungary-ukraine-eu-accession-blocked/)
- Cluster 1: opened 2026-06-15, after Magyar lifted the veto in exchange for minority-rights commitments. [Hromadske](https://hromadske.ua/en/world/265229-pershyy-klaster-shchodo-vstupu-ukrayiny-v-yes-mozut-vidkryty-vze-15-chervnia-uhorshchyna-skasuvala-veto-ft)
- Cluster 6: Hungary unblocked it on 2026-07-03, Coreper approved on 07-10, and it opened on 07-14. That is about a week from unblocking to Coreper. [Razom](https://razomua.media/en/news/politika/klaster-6-dlya-ukrayiny-uhorshchyna-vidstupyla-chotyry-inshi-dosi-zablokovani)
- Clusters 2 and 3: Hungary blocked the screening results from before July, including repeated refusals in September, until 2026-10-07. That is roughly three months or more, and the block lifted only after a concrete legislative concession from Kyiv. [Euronews](https://www.euronews.com/2026/09/09/another-hungarian-veto-slows-ukraines-eu-accession-process), [European Pravda](https://www.eurointegration.com.ua/eng/news/2026/10/7/7247137/)
- What this suggests: once Hungary lifts a block, Coreper has acted within 0 to 7 days. The blocks themselves have lasted weeks to months. The block on clusters 4 and 5 is now about three weeks old, and Hungary has named no concrete condition.

## 5. Other forecasts

- I found no market on this specific question.
- Related markets, which are only loosely connected:
  - Polymarket, "Ukraine signs EU accession treaty by Dec 31, 2027": 6.5% Yes.
  - Manifold, same question: 27%. [Manifold](https://manifold.markets/Xaniguane/will-ukraine-sign-an-eu-accession-t)
  - Kalshi, "Ukraine becomes EU associate member before 2027": 6%.
- None of these measures Coreper approval of screening results for clusters 4 and 5.

## 6. Upcoming events before January 1, 2027

- Weekly COELA meetings through mid-December are chances for Hungary to change its position. It was asked on October 20, October 27 and November 10.
- The Ukraine-Hungary intergovernmental commission is due to start work in November; I have no confirmed date.
- The December General Affairs Council and the December European Council are the usual setting for enlargement decisions and intergovernmental conferences. I did not verify their exact 2026 dates.
- The Commission's enlargement package, which ties into the December Council conclusions, could be used to add pressure.
- Note on scope: the question only needs Coreper approval of the screening results, not the formal opening of the clusters. Going by clusters 2, 3 and 6, Coreper could act within days of Hungary dropping its objection.

As of November 11, 2026, Coreper (the committee of EU ambassadors, whose approval decides this question) has not approved the screening results for Ukraine's clusters 4 and 5. Hungary has now blocked them at three straight meetings of the enlargement working party (COELA), the step before Coreper. Cluster 4 is the green agenda and sustainable connectivity; cluster 5 is resources, agriculture and cohesion. Because the question asks only about Coreper approval, nothing before 2027 has settled it yet.

## 1. Resolution source
- No single data series decides this. It turns on credible reports of Coreper approving the screening results. The usual order is: COELA approves, Coreper agrees, Ukraine is invited to submit negotiating positions, and an intergovernmental conference (IGC) then formally opens the clusters.
- 2026-11-10: Latest status is not approved. At the November 10 COELA meeting, Hungary refused again; an EU diplomat called its position "No change." [Ukrainska Pravda](https://www.pravda.com.ua/eng/news/2026/11/10/8062207/), [European Pravda](https://www.eurointegration.com.ua/news/2026/11/10/7249710/)
- 2026-11-04: The Commission's 2026 Ukraine report says clusters 4 and 5 still have to be opened. [EC report](https://enlargement.ec.europa.eu/document/download/c817ca8c-4ddf-405d-896a-40becd42924a_en?filename=ukraine-report-2026.pdf)
- I did not fetch the cluster definition links given in the question.

## 2. Current status
- Not settled. Hungary refused at COELA on 2026-10-20, 2026-10-27 and 2026-11-10. [Interfax-Ukraine](https://en.interfax.com.ua/news/general/1223387.html), [UNITED24](https://united24media.com/world/hungary-keeps-ukraines-last-two-eu-accession-negotiating-clusters-frozen-23840), [Ukrainska Pravda](https://www.pravda.com.ua/eng/news/2026/11/10/8062207/)
- Moldova's screening results for clusters 4 and 5 were blocked too. The two countries' files appear to move together.

## 3. Recent news (newest first)
- 2026-11-10: Hungary blocked again at COELA, position "unchanged." [NV](https://english.nv.ua/nation/hungary-continues-to-stall-ukraine-s-eu-accession-talks-50658084.html), [ZMINA](https://zmina.info/en/news-en/hungary-again-blocks-screening-results-for-two-clusters-in-ukraines-eu-accession-talks/)
- 2026-11-04: Deputy Prime Minister Chentsov said Hungary is raising no new demands on minority rights. Budapest says it needs more time to study the documents. He is aiming for "November or December." [European Pravda](https://www.eurointegration.com.ua/news/2026/11/10/7249710/), [Interfax](https://en.interfax.com.ua/news/general/1219529.html)
- 2026-11-03: Ukraine's EU envoy Taras Kachka said Hungary has "no substantive requirements, disagreements or concerns." He said the minority-education dispute is resolved and he is confident the clusters will open by the end of 2026. [European Pravda](https://www.eurointegration.com.ua/eng/news/2026/11/3/7249180/)
- 2026-10-27: Hungary refused again. Diplomats said the Irish presidency knew beforehand that Budapest would not move. One called putting the item back on the agenda "primarily political," meant to pressure Hungary rather than get a breakthrough. [Ukragroconsult](https://ukragroconsult.com/en/news/hungary-continues-to-block-opening-of-agricultural-cluster-for-ukraine/), [Ukrainska Pravda](https://www.pravda.com.ua/eng/news/2026/10/27/8059933/)
- 2026-10-20: First reported Hungarian refusal at COELA on clusters 4 and 5. No reasons were given. [Interfax](https://en.interfax.com.ua/news/general/1223387.html)
- 2026-10-13: Clusters 2 and 3 were opened at an IGC. This came after Ukraine amended its minority-language education law. [UNITED24](https://united24media.com/world/hungary-keeps-ukraines-last-two-eu-accession-negotiating-clusters-frozen-23840)
- 2026-10-07: Hungary lifted its block on clusters 2 and 3. COELA approved their screening results, and ambassadors invited Ukraine and Moldova to submit negotiating positions. [European Pravda](https://www.eurointegration.com.ua/eng/news/2026/10/7/7247137/)
- 2026-05-22 onward: The Magyar government banned most Ukrainian farm imports. That is relevant context for cluster 5 (agriculture), but no source I found links it to the veto. [Search summary citing UNITED24](https://united24media.com/world/hungary-reinstates-import-ban-on-ukrainian-agricultural-products-19102)
- 2026-06-18: Prime Minister Magyar doubted the remaining clusters could be opened urgently. [Ukrainska Pravda](https://www.pravda.com.ua/eng/news/2026/06/18/8040047/)

## 4. Base rates
- Hungary has repeatedly held up Ukraine's procedural steps. Reports describe a veto of about 17 months that was lifted around 2026-06-04 [Interfax](https://en.interfax.com.ua/news/general/1223387.html). The block on clusters 2 and 3 lasted from about the summer (Euronews, 2026-09-09) to 2026-10-07, and was lifted only once a specific condition was met (the education law).
- Once Hungary agreed, the steps moved quickly. COELA and Coreper both approved around 2026-10-07, and the IGC was held 6 days later. So a lifted block could plausibly lead to Coreper approval within days.
- The difference this time: Hungary has stated no substantive condition, only that it needs "time to study." That gives no clear trigger for when it might lift the block.

## 5. Other forecasts
- I found no market on this specific question.
- Related markets, all only loosely relevant:
  - Polymarket, "Ukraine signs an EU accession treaty by end of 2027": 6.5% Yes.
  - Manifold, the same question: 27%. [Manifold](https://manifold.markets/Xaniguane/will-ukraine-sign-an-eu-accession-t)
  - Kalshi, "Ukraine becomes an EU associate member before 2027": 6%.
  - The other markets in the feed (TPS, unemployment, peace deal and so on) don't bear on this question.
- Ukrainian officials (Kachka, Chentsov) publicly expect the clusters to open by the end of 2026. These are interested parties.

## 6. Upcoming events before resolution
- More COELA meetings, which appear to come roughly every one to two weeks (Oct 20, Oct 27, Nov 10), plus weekly Coreper meetings through December. I could not confirm specific agenda dates.
- The Irish Council presidency ends 2026-12-31, which creates an incentive to try for an IGC in December. I found no IGC date for clusters 4 and 5.
- The December General Affairs Council and the December European Council summit (mid-December, exact dates not verified) are the typical moments for enlargement deals.
- Watch for any bilateral deal between Hungary and Ukraine, for example on agricultural trade or minority issues, or for Hungary announcing it has finished its document review.

forecasts.reasoning:
(a) About 7 weeks remain, from Nov 11 to Dec 31, 2026. For Yes, Coreper must approve the screening results for both cluster 4 and cluster 5 before January 1, 2027. In practice that requires Hungary to lift its block at the enlargement working party (COELA) first. On past patterns, Coreper then follows within 0 to 7 days.

(b) If nothing changes, the answer is No. Hungary has blocked the results at COELA three times (Oct 20, Oct 27, Nov 10), and its position on Nov 10 was described as "No change."

(c) Base rate: under Magyar in 2026, Hungary has lifted every procedural block on Ukraine's clusters eventually. The durations varied:
- Cluster 6 cleared fairly quickly.
- Clusters 2 and 3 were blocked for roughly three or more months and cleared only after a concrete legislative concession from Kyiv.

For a block that is three weeks old, the chance it is lifted within the next seven weeks is roughly 35 to 45%.

(d) Evidence for Yes:
- Kachka (Nov 3) said Hungary has "no substantive requirements, disagreements or concerns" and expects opening by end-2026.
- Chentsov (Nov 4) said Hungary is raising no new minority-rights demands and is targeting "November or December."
- A Ukraine-Hungary intergovernmental commission is due to start work in November.
- The December European Council, the General Affairs Council and the end of the Irish presidency create deadline pressure.
- Coreper moves fast once a block is lifted.

Evidence for No:
- Three consecutive refusals with "no change."
- Diplomats said the presidency knew beforehand that Budapest would not move, and re-listing the item was mainly to apply pressure.
- Magyar said in June that the remaining clusters could not be opened urgently, and Budapest opposes any "fast track."
- Cluster 5 covers agriculture, and Hungary reinstated its Ukrainian farm import ban in May. This is a domestically sensitive issue.
- Both clusters are required. Hungary could split them and approve only cluster 4.
- With no stated condition, there is no clear trigger for unblocking.

(e) No scenario: Hungary keeps citing "study time" and links cluster 5 to agricultural trade terms. December passes with only Council conclusions urging progress, and the item moves to the Cypriot/Lithuanian presidency in 2027.

Yes scenario: the intergovernmental commission produces a package, perhaps on trade or minority implementation. Hungary clears both clusters at COELA in early December, Coreper approves the same week, and an IGC is held before Christmas.

(f) I start at about 40%. The officials who say there are no substantive objections are interested parties and their optimism is a known pattern, so it adds little. Against that, the possible agricultural linkage and the requirement for both clusters pull the estimate down slightly. I settle at about 35%.

Probability: 35%

(a) About seven weeks remain, until January 1, 2027. For Yes, Hungary must drop its objection at COELA, the enlargement working party. Coreper, the committee of EU ambassadors, must then approve the screening results for both cluster 4 (green agenda) and cluster 5 (agriculture and cohesion) before year-end, and credible outlets must report it.

(b) The status quo is No. Hungary has blocked these results at COELA three times: October 20, October 27 and November 10. Its position is described as "No change."

(c) Base rate: in 2026, Hungarian blocks under Magyar have lasted from about a week (cluster 6) to more than three months (clusters 2 and 3). Clusters 2 and 3 were only released after a concrete legislative concession from Kyiv. Once a block lifts, Coreper acts within 0 to 7 days. For a block that is three weeks old with seven weeks left, roughly 35 to 45% of comparable blocks would resolve within the window.

(d) Evidence:
- **For Yes:**
  - On November 3, Ukraine's EU envoy Kachka said Hungary has "no substantive requirements, disagreements or concerns" and expects the clusters to open by end-2026.
  - On November 4, Deputy PM Chentsov said Hungary raises no new minority demands, only "time to study," and he targets November or December.
  - The Irish presidency ends December 31, which gives it an incentive to hold an intergovernmental conference in December.
  - The December General Affairs Council and European Council are the natural moments for a package deal.
  - A Ukraine-Hungary intergovernmental commission is due to start in November.
- **For No:**
  - Hungary refused three times with no movement, and diplomats said putting the item on the agenda was mainly about pressure, not an expected breakthrough (October 27).
  - Cluster 5 covers agriculture, and Hungary has banned Ukrainian farm imports since May. Farmers are a sensitive constituency for Magyar.
  - Magyar has said he opposes any fast track and doubted the remaining clusters could be opened urgently (June 18).
  - Hungary has stated no condition, so there is no clear trigger for lifting the block.
  - Ukrainian officials are interested parties and have been over-optimistic before.

(e) Scenarios:
- **No:** Hungary keeps citing its document review, ties cluster 5 to agricultural trade safeguards, and nothing moves before the holidays. The file passes to the 2027 presidency.
- **Yes:** After the intergovernmental commission meets and with pressure building toward the December summit, Hungary lifts its objection in early to mid December. COELA and Coreper approve the same week, and an intergovernmental conference follows before Christmas.

(f) I start from about 40%. The soft framing of "time to study," with no new demands, and the incentive of the December deadline push slightly upward. The agriculture sensitivity, Magyar's stated opposition to a fast track, and the lack of any progress over three meetings push down. Taken together they roughly cancel out, and I stay near the base rate.

Probability: 38%
